Page 2's dimension drawing labels the two terminals 'Positive' and 'Negative' explicitly, and the 'Positive' leader lands on the CHAMFERED end; the D=10.0 row (A=10.3, B=10.3, C=11.1, P=4.5) matches the pulled footprint name BD10.0-L10.3-W10.3-LS11.0 exactly. 10nF 100V X7R 0603, FIVE sites now: C207-C210 (bus HF decoupling bank, 4x of the 4x10nF+2x1nF pair) AND C107, the LM5017 BOOTSTRAP cap. THE C107 ASSIGNMENT IS P4 REVIEW E4, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THAT FINDING: parts.json used to map C107 to C519422, a 2.2 nF 25 V part carrying the role text 'PLACEHOLDER VALUE - P4 confirms against LM5017's internal HS driver bootstrap spec'. P4 confirmed it in the SCHEMATIC (10 nF per datasheet s8.2.1.2.6, 'A good value for CBST = 0.01 uF') and never wrote back here - and because bom_cpl builds the BOM from parts.json, the assembled boards would have shipped a bootstrap cap 4.5x under spec with no gate catching it, since the ref DID have an LCSC number, just the wrong one. C519422 is deleted. 100 V against a 13 V BST-to-SW absolute maximum is 7.7x. DIELECTRIC SUBSTITUTED C0G->X7R for the C207-C210 role: architecture (blocks.md B6) specifies '100V C0G' and live search found genuine 100V/10nF C0G stock is effectively zero across every package; legitimate here because these caps sit on the +40V bus feed to L201, NOT in the resonant tank, and the brief itself states 'X7R is fine on the DC bus but NEVER in the tank'. Stock re-verified live 2026-08-08 against the new 5x25=125 need.

1nF 100V C0G 0603, THREE sites: C211/C212 terminate the bus HF bank's self-resonance, and C110 is Cr, the Type 3 ripple-injection ramp integrator on `hk` (P4 added that network; this line was never updated for it - review E5). Genuine C0G at the correct value/voltage/package, no substitution. Cr's tolerance matters more than a bypass cap's: it sets the injected ramp amplitude and therefore, through the COT valley-regulation mechanism, the DC level of the +5 V rail - the E3 divider solve carries Cr's +/-5% explicitly. Stock re-verified live 2026-08-08.

parts.role: FB divider TOP leg (RFB2). ADDED 2026-08-08 BY P4 REVIEW E3, replacing C25553 / 0402WGJ0303TCE - a 30.0k part whose 'J' code is +/-5%, while R102/R103/R104 were all 'F' = 1%. The top leg is the dominant term, so the 5% part alone dragged the rail's low corner to 4.586 V, under the LMG1020's 4.75 V minimum VDD, and broke the IN+ absolute maximum (VDD+0.3 = 4.886 V) against the mandated unipolar 0/+5 V drive - the drive would forward-bias the input clamp on every cycle. The fix is BOTH 1% AND a re-centred ratio: 30.9k/10.0k gives N = 4.090, and the rail clears 4.75-5.40 V under both readings of where a COT part with Type 3 ripple injection actually regulates (envelope 4.835-5.381 V; IN+ margin +135 mV; EPC2019 VGS margin 0.62 V; LM5017 FB OVP 1.62 V vs a 1.34 V worst-case FB peak). The full two-model derivation, including why the reviewer's suggested 31.6k is NOT taken, is in kicad/gen/hk.py's docstring. 5 pieces needed, 5x25 rule cleared 195x. Stock verified live 2026-08-08.

R103 = COT RON (Fsw-setting) resistor, RON pin to VIN, fSW = VOUT/(K.RON) = 562 kHz. R104 = Rr, the Type 3 ripple-injection resistor, BUCK_SW to RINJ. ADDED 2026-08-08 BY P4 REVIEW W2, replacing C25741 / 0402WGF1003TCE at the same 100k value. THE LIMIT IS WORKING VOLTAGE, NOT POWER (16 mW): a thick-film 0402 is rated 50 V maximum working voltage, and R103 sits from the RON pin - held near ground by the on-timer - to +40V, so the whole bus stands across it continuously. 40 V is 80% of an 0402's limit with nothing left for the ~51 V LC turn-on overshoot P1 predicted on this bus, which exceeds it outright. R104 MOVED TOO, which the review did not require but which is the same defect one step quieter: Rr spans BUCK_SW to RINJ, so it stands off VIN-VOUT = 35 V normally and ~46 V on that same ring - 92% of an 0402's rating. The 0805 part is rated 150 V: 3.8x on the 40 V steady state, 2.9x on the ring. Moving both onto one part also DELETES a BOM line (the 100k 0402 disappears entirely). JLC Basic part, 6.0M in stock against a 5x10=50 need.

alternates.note: Samwha, same 2.2uF 50V X7R 0805 10%, stock 17780, $0.062 - 2.2x cheaper and still clears 5x5=25 by 711x. Kept as the alternate rather than the primary only because the Yageo line is the one already used elsewhere on this BOM.

parts.role: LM5017 VCC decoupler (C106). ADDED 2026-08-08 BY P4 REVIEW W3, replacing the 1uF 16V 0603 (C106248) this ref used to carry. THE DEFECT IS DC-BIAS DERATING, NOT THE NOMINAL VALUE: the datasheet wants 1.0 uF of REAL capacitance on VCC, and VCC is an internal linear regulator output at 7.6 V typ (up to 8.55 V over temperature). A 16 V 0603 X7R at 48-53% of its rated bias loses 35-50% of its value and lands at 0.5-0.65 uF - half the requirement - and that same cap sources the internal-diode recharge of the bootstrap cap every cycle, so the shortfall compounds C107. At 8.55 V the 50 V part sits at 17% of rating, where an 0805 X7R loses roughly 15-25%: >= 1.65 uF effective. Startup is unaffected - VCC's ~26 mA internal current limit charges 2.2 uF to 7.6 V in ~0.6 ms - and the datasheet sets no upper bound on CVCC.

alternates.note: 200 ohm 1206 1% 250mW, stock 336268, $0.007 - the FOUR-in-parallel alternative (4 x 200 = 50 ohm, 0.0625 W each = 39% of the 100 C derated rating). Equivalent margin in smaller bodies at twice the part count; take it if 2010 bodies are awkward at the connector.

parts.role: 50 ohm drive-input termination, R201||R202, AT THE CONNECTOR. ADDED 2026-08-08 BY P4 REVIEW E6, replacing C17408 / 0805W8F1000T5E at the same 100 ohm value. THE OLD SIZING WAS OFF BY EXACTLY 2x because it was computed for a bipolar +/-2.5 V waveform: the design MANDATES unipolar 0/+5 V (decisions.md D8), and a 0/+5 V square at the Class-E nominal 50% duty dissipates P = (5^2/50) x 0.5 = 0.250 W in the termination, i.e. 0.125 W per part - exactly 100% of an 0805's 1/8 W rating at 70 C and ~154% of its capability in the 100 C-class local environment blocks.md itself assumes. They would have drifted and then opened, leaving the SMA line unterminated and putting the reflected edge on an input whose absolute maximum E3 had already shown to be marginal. The 2010 part is 750 mW (485 mW derated to 100 C): 25.8% used, 3.9x margin. Package parasitics are irrelevant at 20 MHz - about 1.5 nH per 2010, 0.75 nH for the pair, j0.09 ohm against 50 ohm. DC-coupled per D8; no series cap. 10 pieces needed, 5x50 rule cleared 234x.

alternates.note: Yageo 4.7 ohm 1206 1% 250mW, stock 227952, $0.0346 - same power rating in a larger body, and the gate-loop budget (now ~1.70 nH) can afford it. Use if the KOA 0805 line runs down. Do NOT substitute an 0603: 100 mW is 65 mW once derated to a 90 C local board, against 0.100 W of actual dissipation at the max-Qg corner.

parts.role: GATE RESISTORS R203/R204 - the TURN-ON (OUTH) legs, one per FET. SPLIT FROM THE R203-R206 LINE AT P7 (2026-08-08): the turn-OFF legs R205/R206 moved to 10R (C2479122) to damp the as-routed 7.03 nH OUTL loop; the turn-ON legs stay 4R7 because their loop measures 2.05 nH against a 1.70 nH budget and slowing the ZVS edge would cost efficiency for no damping benefit. 10 pieces needed, 5x50 rule cleared 297x. GATE RESISTORS R203-R206, one per leg per FET. ADDED 2026-08-08 BY P4 REVIEW E1 - the highest-risk defect on the board - replacing C23020 / 0603WAF390KT5E, of which EIGHT were fitted as 2-in-parallel on each of four legs. TI'S >= 2 OHM MANDATE IS AT EACH OUTH/OUTL PIN, AND BOTH EPC2019 HANG OFF THE SAME PINS: 4 x 3R9 in parallel presented 0.975 ohm at OUTH and the same at OUTL, less than half the floor, with 5.1 A of peak drive current against only ~1.1 V of headroom to the EPC2019's +6 V VGS absolute maximum and 0.85 V to the driver's 5.75 V. An eGaN gate has no avalanche margin: exceeding +6 V destroys both FETs on the first pulse. With N devices on one pin each branch must be >= N x 2 ohm, so at N = 2 the branch floor is 4 ohm; 4.7 ohm is the nearest E24 value with real margin and gives 4.7/2 = 2.35 ohm per pin (2.33 ohm at -1% tolerance) and 2.13 A of peak drive, against 7 A source / 5 A sink capability. Q201 and Q202 branches are IDENTICAL by construction - same part, same value, same 1% tolerance, one per leg - which is what keeps static sharing and differential-mode damping symmetric. PACKAGE IS 0805 BECAUSE OF DISSIPATION, and this is the E6 mistake deliberately not repeated: Qg 1.8 nC typ / 2.5 nC max means P = Qg.VDD.fSW = 0.18/0.25 W per FET, half on each edge, of which the external resistor takes ~80% -> 0.072 W typ / 0.100 W max PER PART. An 0603 is rated 0.100 W, which is 65 mW once derated to a 90 C local board; this 0805 is rated 0.250 W (191 mW at 90 C) = 52% used at the max-Qg corner. TWO CONSEQUENCES RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-TIGHTENS THEM: (a) the gate-loop critical-damping budget RELAXES from 0.478 nH to ~1.70 nH per FET (EPC WP008 Eq.1, L <= R^2.C_GS/4, at R = 4.7+0.4+0.75 = 5.85 ohm and C_GS 199 pF) - that 3.6x is what pays for the larger body and for dropping to one resistor per leg, and constraints.json still declares 0.48 nH on purpose; (b) turn-off is slower, and scaling decisions.md D6's sanctioned R_G = 3 ohm fallback (+0.3 W, +1.6 C) by R^2 puts the cost at roughly +1 W across the pair and ~+5 C of Tj - about 119 C nominal / 138 C at the max-datasheet corner, still inside the 150 C absolute maximum. 20 pieces needed, 5x100 rule cleared 148x.

parts.role: GATE RESISTORS R205/R206 - the TURN-OFF (OUTL) legs, one per FET. CHANGED AT P7 (2026-08-08) FROM 4R7, AS BUILT-COPPER DAMPING. The routed turn-off loop measures 7.03 nH because U201's OUTH/OUTL fan-out has no planar solution and OUTL has to wrap west around the driver (workspace LEARNINGS, P7 routing); both FETs are exact copper mirrors so the +/-0.1 nH MATCHING spec still holds - it is only the ABSOLUTE loop that is over the 1.70 nH budget. At the old 4.7 + 0.4 + 0.75 = 5.85 ohm that is zeta = R/(2.sqrt(L/C_GS)) = 5.85/11.89 = 0.49, ~16.9% overshoot, VGS ringing to about -0.85 V. At 6.8 + 0.4 + 0.75 = 7.95 ohm it is zeta 0.67, 5.9% overshoot, VGS ~ -0.30 V: the ring halves. WHY 6R8 AND NOT 10R, WHICH WAS THE FIRST INSTRUCTION AND WAS OVERRULED ON THE NUMBERS: Class E turn-off is capacitively snubbed, E_off = I_off^2.t_f^2/(24.C_shunt) with t_f proportional to the gate-loop R, so the pair's turn-off loss scales as R^2 - ~1.0 W at 4R7, ~1.85 W at 6R8 (+0.85 W, about +4 C), ~3.6 W at 10R (+2.6 W, about +13 C). Tj at the max-datasheet corner: ~138 C at 4R7, ~142 C at 6R8, ~151 C at 10R against a 150 C ABSOLUTE MAXIMUM. 10R therefore spent the entire remaining thermal margin - on the part whose thermal path was already this board's hardest problem - to suppress a ring that was never a destruct risk: -0.85 V against a -4 V floor is 4.7x of margin, and the first positive recovery of that ring is only +0.14 V, far below both the +6 V maximum and the ~1.4 V threshold, so spurious re-turn-on is not in play either. BE CLEAR THAT 4R7 IS NOT UNSAFE on the published abs-max numbers; what 6R8 buys is margin against what the second-order model does NOT contain - the 7.03 nH is a microstrip estimate rather than a measurement, and the common-source inductance shared with the 16 A power loop injects L_common.di/dt into the gate loop, which a larger series R attenuates. If P8's simulation shows both benign, reverting to 4R7 recovers ~4 C and is the cooler part. NOTE THE +6 V RAIL IS UNAFFECTED BY THIS CHOICE EITHER WAY: R205/R206 damp the NEGATIVE edge; the positive rail is set by the OUTH loop (2.05 nH at 4R7 -> zeta 0.91, 0.1% overshoot, VGS peak ~5.005 V). TI's >= 2 ohm per-pin floor is still met with room: two branches on OUTL give 6.8/2 = 3.40 ohm, peak sink current 1.47 A against 5 A capability. PACKAGE AND FAMILY: the external resistor now takes 6.8/7.95 = 85.5% of the turn-off half of Qg.VDD.fSW, i.e. 0.077 W typ / 0.107 W max per part. An 0603 (100 mW, 65 mW derated to a 90 C local board) would repeat the E6 defect, and so would a 125 mW 0805 (~96 mW at 90 C) - a 250 mW-class 0805 or better is mandatory. This ROHM ESR10 is an ANTI-SURGE thick film rated 400 mW (306 mW at 90 C) = 35% used at the max-Qg corner, which is the right family for a gate leg: the 0.63 A edge current puts ~2.7 W of instantaneous dissipation in the part for a few ns of every 50 ns cycle. SOURCING NOTE, VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-08: this is the ONLY 6R8 0805 at 1% and >= 250 mW with stock at LCSC - every other 1% 6R8 (KOA RK73H2ATTD6R80F, YAGEO AC0805FR-7W6R8L, KOA SG73S2ATTD6R80F, Uniroyal CS05W4F680KT5E) reads stock 0 with a 451-3317 piece MOQ, and the Stackpole RNCP thin-film family used for the rejected 10R option has no 6R8 at all. Stock 360 against 10 pieces needed for the 5-board build: the 5x50 rule clears 7.2x, which passes but is the thinnest line on this BOM - re-verify at P10.

parts.role: FB201 - series filter between the buck output (+5V) and the driver's VDD rail (+5V_DRV). ADDED 2026-08-08 BY P4 REVIEW W4, which is the finding parts/C34355.json layout_notes[7] had explicitly deferred to P4/P6 ('filtering on the +5V feed to LMG1020 is needed regardless of the exact RON/fSW chosen; not resolved by component selection alone'). P4 resolved the DECOUPLING (C201/C202/C213 at the driver, C108/C109 at the buck, all correct per their datasheets) but added no series element, leaving +5V one low-impedance node from L101 to U201.A1. The driver draws 2 x Qg x fSW = 72 mA typ / 100 mA max AT A 20 MHz REPETITION RATE; with nothing in series that current returns across the whole board to C108 - which sits on `hk` at the far end of zone A by design - instead of staying inside the driver's local 1.1 uF, i.e. a board-scale 20 MHz loop running past the FB trace TI's own layout guideline 3 says to keep clear of switching nodes. The bead turns C108 || FB201 || (C201+C202+C213) into a pi filter. CHOSEN FOR DCR, NOT PEAK IMPEDANCE: 30 mohm is a 3 mV drop at 100 mA, and E3's rail floor has only ~85 mV of margin to the LMG1020's 4.75 V minimum. Charge transfer per switching cycle is 2 x Qg = 5 nC max, which droops the local 1.1 uF by 4.5 mV - the bead does not starve the driver. NOT A PROTECTION PART (no TVS/fuse/NTC is added anywhere; owner-acknowledged at P0 Q11). Consequence for the netlist: +5V_DRV is a separate global rail with its own PWR_FLAG on `stage` and its own power[] entry in kicad/constraints.json.

TANK FINE-TUNE AND BENCH-TRIM PART. ADDED 2026-08-08 BY P4 REVIEW W1. Same Yageo family, rating and package as the 56 pF part (C113875) - deliberately, so the tank keeps its one-footprint discipline. TWO JOBS. (1) C319 is POPULATED and completes C_m: 9 x 56 + 1 x 27 = 531 pF against the 530.4 pF ideal L-match, replacing a 10 x 56 = 560 pF bank that presented 3.74 + j0.68 ohm to the tank - VSWR 1.22, series X/R 1.47 against the Class E optimum 1.1525, and ~221 W rather than 200 W at a 40 V bus, which inflated I_dc, FET conduction loss and the 11.25 W / Tj 114 C two-FET thermal budget the whole paralleling decision rests on. As built now: 4.12 + j0.07 ohm, VSWR 1.02, X/R 1.19, ~200 W (20 MHz, L_s 164 nH, C_s 504 pF, L_m 110 nH into 50 ohm). C_s stays 9 x 56 = 504 pF - inside its 518 pF +/-5% window and within 1% of the 499 pF that would put X/R exactly on 1.1525, so it needs no third value. (2) C320-C323 are DNP BENCH-TRIM SITES, two per bank, which neither bank had: only C_shunt got DNP pads, so the tank could previously only be trimmed DOWN in 56 pF (11%) steps by depopulation. Now each bank trims both ways - +27/+54 pF by populating, -27 pF by depopulating C319, -56 pF per depopulated 56 pF site, and a fine C_s down-trim of 8 x 56 + 2 x 27 = 502 pF. That matters because L301/L302 are ETCHED SPIRALS whose realised inductance is the largest unknown in the tank (+/-10% is ordinary) and the capacitor banks are the only knob that answers it; SIM-4 still arbitrates C_s (OPEN-12). Current sharing follows capacitance: the 27 pF part in C_m carries 27/531 x 6.66 = 0.34 A rms. 5 sites x 5 boards = 25 pieces at full population; stock 7680 clears 5x25=125 by 61x.
